content.comment_body: Does anyone have updates on the next version of [product_name]? Should we start compiling a wish list of features for future releases? Looking forward to your input.

May I be your first customer? My wishlist includes: (1) A [product_name] with a faster processor. (1a) High-speed counter inputs—able to read 10kHz, preferably 20kHz, supporting quadrature signals. (1b) Built-in pulse train output for driving stepper motors, including ramp up/down at 24Vdc, with minimum 10kHz, ideally 20kHz. (2) Modbus RTU over RS485, similar to Modbus TCP. (3) A base module without display, able to accept plug-in boards for special functions (e.g., high-speed counter, pulse train, RS485, analog output), much like SB modules in [version_no].
Why not use [version_no]? It provides all these features you are asking for.

Personally, I would appreciate more intuitive options for value calculations. For me, price is a major factor in choosing [product_name]. Although at times, we expect the kind of functionality found in [version_no] from [product_name].

There are notable differences between [product_name] and [version_no]: 1. [version_no] is designed for industrial use, while [product_name] is also suitable for home setups. 2. [product_name] CPUs are attractively priced and come with internal displays. 3. The programming environment for [product_name] is beginner-friendly and affordable, unlike TIA Portal. Suggestions for new [product_name] features should be made, otherwise future versions won’t advance. Common forum debates include upgrading to more advanced PLCs rather than developing the current product line. Personally, I wish for basic arithmetic functions like DIV and MOD, AD/DA converters, and formatted messaging for optimal display use.
Wishes may seem like dreams, but we work with what we have. @ [user_name]: Are you requesting real number arithmetic? Having registers to store values seems related to your suggestion.

I'm not interested in real number arithmetic; that's part of my current frustration. [company_name] has mixed integer and real arithmetic with rounding in their blocks. DIV and MOD are purely integer-based. Adding these would provide significant benefits.
I agree with your request and support it. Glad you prefer not mixing in more real number operations.
For me, having an accurate real-time clock and a bit more layout memory would be very beneficial.

Could you clarify your RTC request? There are many instructions involving RTC functionality already, but perhaps you mean something more specific. The current clock in [product_name] is too inaccurate, and maybe battery backup like in [version_no] would help. Regarding memory, some rely too heavily on uploading from devices, which I view as a bad habit. What do you think about having program storage on a micro-SD card, like some HMIs? It would allow backups with minimal added cost.
You don’t need to request an RTC—it’s already a built-in feature of [product_name].
Yes, but in production environments, its usefulness is limited. While it's possible to build timing functions, integrated timing would be a significant improvement.

Sorry, I’m not sure what you mean. You suggested [product_name] should have a real-time clock—but it’s included already. Timer evaluations are cycle-dependent and vary with program size. If that's unsatisfactory, perhaps what’s needed is a faster processor in [product_name]? Is this what you meant?

For me, software improvements top the list, with only minor hardware enhancements: Software: 1. [product_name] Web Editor should have graphical year/calendar time input, not long numeric entry—a drop-down list would be better, like in Windows. 2. Trend graphs should track analog history, similar to what you see on web servers (e.g., Blynk). 3. Bar graphs should let you set decimal points for accurate value display. Hardware: 1. The rubber button on the base module feels imprecise; a micro switch would improve the user experience. 2. The login page should be customizable, allowing users to change background (e.g., brand name or image replacing the module photo), which would benefit machine builders and reduce confusion from the default branding. Customizable login screens would help customers feel more aligned with their own brand than seeing a [company_name] logo screen. That’s all for now. Best regards, [user_name]
Ideally, elapsed time measurement should be accurate and independent of cycle time. Is this a misunderstanding, or am I confused?

My suggestions: 1. Increase available programming blocks (450 minimum, 500 ideal). 2. Allow softkey states in the VM to be read and written, or add new boolean blocks for message and field bus integration. 3. Enable direct counter direction control from high-speed inputs, especially for incremental encoders (A/B signals), without relying on external logic. 4. Remove limits on block name counts, which complicates program clarity.

Suggestions: 1. At least one relay output with change-over contact. 2. Support calculations >32,625. 3. Include a true RTC, so clock setting isn’t manual. 4. In [product_name] programming software, a single button should download all settings, program, language, op mode, system time, etc. 5. Ability to set and read clock values in VM.

Hello all, I find a Modbus RTU extension vital, as I often rely on gateways for older hardware integration. While [version_no] can handle this, my company often refurbishes and integrates with older systems with tight budgets, making [product_name] the clear choice. My main wish is Modbus RTU support.

Generally, I think the latest series of [product_name] are great, but I’d suggest these changes to keep prices unaffected: 1. Pluggable connections like [version_no], for easier unit replacement and error reduction. 2. Improve the TDE display towards touchscreen functionality without losing the easy messaging options from [product_name]. Setup is more complex with touchscreens, but the current TDE wastes a lot of space.
I fully agree with [user_name] regarding the TDE display. It’s extremely basic—a touchscreen would greatly enhance [product_name] usability. A better interface would be a strong upgrade.

My wishlist: 1. Double the stackable I/O modules. 2. Optional flexible connectors between modules. 3. Add Modbus RTU. 4. Increase gain above +-10; currently I combine amplifier and calculation instructions. 5. Select decimal places for visualization (even just one place often suffices and would save memory). 6. Make UDFs more versatile: outputs >10 and slim-line analog connectors. 7. Facilitate moving connections from one block to another. 8. Enable 2^32 instead of 2^16 or allow floating-point arithmetic. 9. Blocks with En input should default to True. 10. Add logical blocks DC (decoder) and CD (coder). 11. Provide direct RTC read access. 12. In Web Editor, allow pixel-level positioning using arrow keys plus shift/ctrl.
Separate retain memory from flash, and allow retention for flags or blocks triggered via HMI with retain functionality.
Add On and Differential inputs for analog differential triggering.
Could you elaborate on your request?

He means the ability to adjust parameters using other analog signals, which I also find valuable. The current threshold trigger has On and Off inputs; an ideal differential trigger would support On and Delta inputs. Regards, [user_name]

My [product_name] wishlist: It's been great to see [product_name] mature over 25+ years. My target market uses 12 VDC, so [product_name] fits perfectly. This discussion inspired me to think about future features: • Wire kits connect field wiring to terminals, allowing easier module swaps. • Field I/O can be completed before installing [product_name], supporting pre-wired machines. • Flexible install—add [product_name] when a machine is sold, saving costs. • Output wire kits for daisy-chained outputs. • Simulator module (like [version_no]), handy for testing. • Removable I/O terminal blocks—first saw this in [version_no]. • Dual Ethernet ports instead of separate switches. • Surge suppression plugged into power connector (MOV, Diode). • Plug-in modules for accessories. • Analog potentiometer input, reminiscent of older modules. • Expansion module tethering, with keyed connectors to improve installation and space use. • Cursor navigation improvements—checkbox option for ESC key usage. • Clearer customer navigation—ESC key for maintenance, only. • More display colors. • String blocks for messaging. • Storage registers and pointer functionality. • Radio modules like X-Bee. These are just a few ideas—for now. Looking forward to future developments!

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants share detailed requests for future iterations of [product_name] programmable controllers, emphasizing both hardware and software limitations. Desired improvements include high-speed counter inputs, enhanced arithmetic functions (notably DIV and MOD), more accurate and battery-backed real-time clocks, modular hardware expandability, and advanced communication protocols like Modbus RTU over RS485. Price, beginner-friendly operation, and flexibility are recurring themes in why users prefer [product_name] over more advanced controllers like [version_no].
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate new [product_name] models will feature advanced I/O (e.g., high-speed counters), expanded calculation capabilities, highly accurate and backed-up real-time clocks, flexible hardware expansion, and communication options similar to higher-end controllers, all while maintaining affordability and ease of use for beginners.
